title: WHO Primary Health Care
text:
Primary health care is a whole-of-society approach to health
that aims to ensure the highest possible level of health and
well-being and equitable distribution.

Primary health care includes integrated health services,
health promotion, disease prevention, treatment,
rehabilitation and palliative care.

It also addresses broader determinants of health and
empowers individuals, families and communities.

title: WHO Diabetes
text:
Diabetes is a chronic metabolic disease characterized by
elevated blood glucose levels.

Diabetes can cause serious damage to the heart, blood vessels,
eyes, kidneys and nerves.

Healthy diet, physical activity, maintaining a healthy body
weight and avoiding tobacco are important components of
reducing risk and managing health.

People with diabetes may require ongoing medical care,
monitoring and management under appropriate healthcare
guidance.

title: WHO Hypertension
text:
Hypertension is high blood pressure.

Many people with hypertension may not experience obvious
symptoms, which is why blood pressure measurement is important.

Uncontrolled hypertension can increase the risk of
cardiovascular disease and other serious health complications.

Appropriate diagnosis and management should involve
qualified healthcare professionals.

title: WHO Mental Health
text:
Mental health is an important component of overall health
and well-being.

Mental health conditions can affect thoughts, emotions,
behaviour and daily functioning.

Mental health concerns should be assessed in context,
and people experiencing significant or persistent symptoms
may require professional healthcare support.
